newsitem.title: UK: Clarke says strength of sterling is "dramatic".
newsitem.headline: Clarke says strength of sterling is "dramatic".

text.p: The dramatic rise in sterling is the biggest problem facing British manufacturers and exporters, ex-chancellor of the exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Thursday.
"A three mark pound is staring us in the face," Clarke told a parliamentary debate on the budget.
Clarke blamed the pound's sharp rise on a combination of fiscal tightening by Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown and monetary tightening by Bank of England Governor Eddie George.

"There's one constraint that is already staring him (Brown) in the face, and I don't know what they're going to do about it. They have succeeded in sending up the pound to dramatic levels," Clarke said.
He said the government seemed "to be doing everything it can think of to drive the pound up further in the pursuit of its economic policy".
